{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('/home/musel/Github/research_agent/data/trial.csv')

# Check for sentinel values in biomarker_baseline
sentinel_count = (df['biomarker_baseline'] == -999).sum()
print(f'Number of sentinel values (-999) in biomarker_baseline: {sentinel_count}')

# Check for duplicate patient_ids
duplicate_count = df['patient_id'].duplicated().sum()
print(f'Number of duplicate patient_id entries: {duplicate_count}')

# Check for multiple sample_seq per patient
duplicates_by_id = df[df['patient_id'].duplicated(keep=False)].groupby('patient_id')['sample_seq'].count()
print(f'Number of patients with multiple sample_seq: {len(duplicates_by_id)}')
print(f'Max sample_seq per patient: {duplicates_by_id.max()}')

# Note: This confirms 24 patients have multiple sample_seq (from 848 rows - 800 unique patient_ids = 48 rows extra → 24 patients tested twice)

# Check the distribution of assay_batch
print(f'Assay batch A: {df[df["assay_batch"] == "A"].shape[0]} rows')
print(f'Assay batch B: {df[df["assay_batch"] == "B"].shape[0]} rows')

# Confirm: baseline biomarker has no unit issue (only final has batch B unit error)
# So we don't need to adjust biomarker_baseline

# Deduplicate: keep highest sample_seq per patient
# We will drop rows with -999 in baseline, then deduplicate
# First, filter out sentinel values
filtered_df = df[df['biomarker_baseline'] != -999]

# Now deduplicate by highest sample_seq per patient
# Sort by patient_id and sample_seq descending, then drop duplicates
deduplicated_df = filtered_df.sort_values(['patient_id', 'sample_seq'], ascending=[True, False]).drop_duplicates(subset=['patient_id'], keep='first')

# Check final number of patients
print(f'Final number of unique patients after deduplication: {deduplicated_df.shape[0]}')

# Compute mean baseline biomarker
mean_baseline = deduplicated_df['biomarker_baseline'].mean()
print(f'Mean baseline biomarker (ng/mL) across all patients: {mean_baseline:.2f}')"}
